posts.name: Azqa
posts.cooked:
With admittedly limited plays against him, so far they've always come down to only 5 or 6 cards left in the environment deck, so his potential danger has been on his flip side rather than his damage dealing side.  That seems to fit thematically too - he's not really trying to hurt humans so much as he's trying to wreck the world enough that civilizations backslide and we don't continue on the path that results in the cosmic event that destroyed his people.

Even if you destroy one of his ongoings per round, he's going to flip and take 3 environment cards out of the deck about every other round, so he's got an ~10-11 round limit on the game.  He definitely seems like one that'll scale noticeably based on the number of heroes.

posts.cooked:
Follow-up questions about Deadline's flipping:

So, 3 Catastrophes in play at end of turn.  He Flips.   Does his new "end of turn" event on the back side take effect right away, or at the end of his next turn? If it does take effect the same turn he flips, does it happen right away, or does it become the "newest" card in play and therefore the last card of "end of turn" to take effect?

posts.name: Donner
posts.cooked: It is still the end of turn, so the "new" end of turn effect takes place.  Likewise, when the Plague Rat flips at the start of the turn, his start of turn effects on the new side also trigger.

posts.name: phelpsfunk
posts.cooked: Does the new side take place immediately, or does the villain card get moved to the end of the effect chain as "newest card in play"?

posts.name: Pydro
posts.cooked:
It's immediate. The ruling of Order of Operations for Start- and End-of-turn effects is based on when the card as a whole enters play, not the particular text. Since the villain card as a whole (both sides) was in play first, it acts first.

So, after a villain flips, you do not have to remember how many cards came out before it flipped and after it flipped.

Another example is where one of the Ennead that came out later dies first. Even though it flipped first, the incapped ability of an Ennead that entered the battle earlier but died later would trigger first.
